PC: ABC's evaluated (must demonstrate or state that they are evaluating the airway/breathing and circulation)
Obtains suficient history (History including recent chemotherapy, fever,symptoms,medications)
Asks for 10o% oxygen by non-rebreather mask to be applied
Place on monitors (CR and oximetry)
Asks for central line to be accessed
Begins rapid IV fluid bolus (20 cc/kg in <15 min)
Orders labs: at least a CBC and Blood Culture
Ask for bedside glucose check
Orders any broad spectrum antibiotics (e.g. ceftriaxone)
Specifically chooses anti-pseudomonal coverage such as ceftazidime (gets credit for check box above as well)
When told that the bolus is done -no pressure change noted,repeats the bolus
When prompted “Nurse notes child is barely beathing", begins bag-mask ventilation
Recognizes need to intubate
Intubation: Raises bed to appropriate height/positions child
Gathers necessary equipment (ET Tube, laryngoscope, bag/mask - if not done at step above)
Check equipment (suction set to correctpressure, laryngoscope light works)
Suction to bedside
Chooses proper blade size and type (Miller/Mac 2)
Chooses proper endotracheal tube size (5-5.5 uncuffed endotracheal tube)
Choose proper RSI drugs - Atropine,a BPsparing sedative-a low dose of fentanyl,midazolam, etomidate,ketamine,and aparalytic
Has assistant apply cricoid pressure (if not done, patient will vomit during intubation)
Endotracheal tube passed using correct technique (credit for holding blade in correct hand, correct body position-no penalty for “breaking teeth")

Confirms endotracheal tube position: (Resident will be asked to explain his/her method(s) for confirming proper tube placement - if not offered spontaneously) Auscultates chest Auscultates over stomach Evaluates chest rise Asks for end-tidal CO2 monitoring Orders confirmatory chest X-ray
Release cricoid pressure after tubeconfirmation (except for chest X-ray)
Secures endotracheal tube (NG -ok but review risk with low platelets)
Considers third bolus (may have occurred earlier)
Asks for dopamine drip, titrates to 10-20 mcg/kg/min (epinephrine, dobutamine-not first line-no credit)
